title: Asthma care online: inhaler refills and a plan from a doctor by message
summary: Asthma treatment online on FutureClinic is $40 a visit. A doctor reads your case by message and can send inhaler refills and a plan if it's right for you.
body_markdown:
Asthma care by message lets a physician review your symptom control, update your written action plan, and send inhaler refills to your pharmacy. In[AMN Healthcare's May 2025 survey](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2025-05-27-New-Survey-Shows-Physician-Appointment-Wait-Times-Surge-19-Since-2022,-48-Since-2004) of 15 US metros, new-patient physician waits averaged 31 days (23.5 days in family medicine), and GINA notes that poor adherence to daily inhaled steroids leaves some patients on albuterol alone.


Many people seek online care for convenience without getting trapped in[subscriptions](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) or tied to one medication provider. Do you want another service and the requirements attached to it, or do you want an expert doctor of your own? If you want medicines bundled into a subscription, another service is a strong option. If you wanted an expert doctor directly,[FutureClinic](https://futureclinic.com/) gives you that with nothing attached.


On FutureClinic, a specific doctor reads your whole case and answers you one to one, and your plan includes a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded live for you. No form is approved in bulk. If your doctor decides it's right for you, they can send inhaler refills to the pharmacy you choose and write an asthma action plan by message. That same doctor can treat other problems in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


FutureClinic is not for emergencies, and an asthma attack is an emergency: call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.


## Why messaging the same doctor over time matters for asthma


Asthma shifts with seasons and triggers, so messaging the same doctor time after time, however long in between, lets you build trust, try treatments together, and track progress in one chat. Together you can compare home peak expiratory flow (PEF) readings against your personal best, review rescue puffs over the past four weeks, swap an inhaler that causes thrush or hoarseness, or review flare-ups and steroid courses over the past year, stepping down after two to three stable months or stepping up after a flare.


Your doctor's only incentive is to help you. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, so they never upsell a medicine or lab panel. With no subscription required, they can prescribe whichever non-controlled medicine fits you, any brand or generic, to the pharmacy you choose, with no house formulary, including several months of a stable medicine when they judge it safe.


## AI asthma treatment: what a doctor manages by message, and when to go in person


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors on the platform. Generalists and specialists span more than 60 specialties, and every clinician is a state-licensed, background-checked physician with an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. First, an AI assistant trained by the doctors asks about your diagnosis, past spirometry or peak flow numbers, current inhalers, rescue canisters used in the past year, and recent steroid courses or urgent visits. The assistant never gives medical advice. You confirm a summary before the doctor reads the whole conversation and writes back. Real care takes hours, so replies typically come within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next.


Your physician can also treat related conditions in their specialty, such as allergic rhinitis or reflux. In-person care is required for physical exams, clinic spirometry,[FeNO breath tests](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma/diagnosis) , office allergy shots, and the first dose of dust-mite sublingual immunotherapy ([Odactra](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=dermatophagoides) ), per[GINA](https://ginasthma.org/2026-gina-strategy-report/) and[NAEPP 2020](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/resources/2020-focused-updates-asthma-management-guidelines) . If asthma stays uncontrolled at Step 4 despite good technique and adherence, GINA advises referral to a severe-asthma specialist, who may consider a biologic.


## Why current guidelines move away from albuterol alone


The[May 2026 GINA report](https://ginasthma.org/2026-gina-strategy-report/) estimates asthma affects 300 million people worldwide. Because people with infrequent symptoms can still have severe exacerbations, GINA avoids the term "mild asthma" and recommends against treating adults, adolescents, or children 6 to 11 with a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA, like albuterol) alone. Using three or more 200-dose SABA canisters a year is linked to more exacerbations and higher mortality. GINA outlines two tracks (while[NAEPP 2020](https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/resources/2020-focused-updates-asthma-management-guidelines) recommends daily and reliever ICS-formoterol for ages 4 and up with moderate to severe persistent asthma):


-


**Track 1 (ICS-formoterol reliever):** Low-dose budesonide-formoterol is taken as needed at Steps 1 to 2 (55% fewer severe exacerbations and 65% fewer emergency visits or hospitalizations on average versus SABA alone in adult and adolescent trials), or daily plus as needed at Steps 3 to 5 (MART, 32% fewer severe exacerbations on average versus the same ICS-LABA dose). In the US, Symbicort and generic Breyna (approved March 2022) state they are "NOT indicated for the relief of acute bronchospasm," making reliever and MART use guideline-endorsed off-label care (max 12 puffs of 160/4.5 mcg in 24 hours for ages 12 and up; never pair with salmeterol or vilanterol).


-


**Track 2 (ICS-SABA or SABA with an ICS):** Uses as-needed albuterol-budesonide (Airsupra, FDA-approved for adults 18 and up at 2 puffs of 90/80 mcg, max 12 puffs in 24 hours, cutting yearly severe exacerbations by 53% versus albuterol alone in the BATURA trial) or a daily ICS or ICS-LABA with albuterol HFA. Shake suspension inhalers right before each puff. Tiotropium is a Step 5 add-on; montelukast carries a[March 2020 FDA Boxed Warning](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-requires-boxed-warning-about-serious-mental-health-side-effects-asthma-and-allergy-drug) for serious mental health side effects.
